verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left-sided hearing and facial symptoms: "Just one side. Just on my left side. I've noticed that the hearing's kind of gone down a bit" and onset "It's been a few weeks now. About three weeks or something." plus numbness: "my face has been feeling a bit numb recently."
Location of numbness is described as: "it's the left side. It's kind of like around my left ear and kind of along here. So like my jawline sort of feeling a bit numb around here."
Tinnitus and dizziness are noted: clinician says "Some ringing in your ear" and later patient adds "like I said, like the ringing occasionally and when I get back and sometimes feel a bit dizzy."

The patient denies these symptoms: "have you had any weakness or numbness down in the rest of the body at all?" – "No, no, no, no, nothing like that."; "Have you had any difficulty swallowing?" – "No."; "have you had any difficulty speaking?" – "No."; "Have you noticed any problems with your vision at all?" – "No, that's all good."

Ear and systemic negatives: "Do you have any discharge coming from that ear at all?" – "No, nothing coming out."; "Any pain in the ear or from the ear?" – "No."; "have you had any fever at all?" – "Nothing like that."; "Do you have any itchiness in the ear?" is asked but the patient answers about cotton buds; however, there is no report of itchiness, so absence is implied.
History of nasal polyps: "I've got kind of been told I had polyps in my nose in the past."
Remote labyrinthitis: "I think they said ages ago I had something called can't quite remember, but labyrinthitis, something like that."

Nasal spray PRN, name unknown: "if my polyps are playing up, I've got a spray" and later "I only take the spray for my nose when I need it" and "Do you remember the name of the spray at all?" – "Unfortunately, I don't."
Rennie as needed: "occasionally get some Kind of hearty feeling... I take a Rennie's if I need to" and later "sometimes take over like Rennie, but I just get that from the chemist."
Latex allergy: "Do you have any allergies to any medication?" – "No, just latex."
Family history: "My brother had neurofibromatosis. I think it is."
Occupation and impact: "Yeah, so I'm a jockey." and "because of all the kind of symptoms I'm... I've just had to do far less training, so kind of beginning to. Yeah. Impacting work a little bit now."
Living situation: "I live with my partner."
No pets: "Do you have any pets at all at home?" – "No pets."
This was a video consultation and no exam findings are given: "Obviously we're limited in terms of assessment via video portal" and no physical examination findings are documented.

Transcript supports left-sided hearing reduction and facial numbness of subacute ("about three weeks") onset, but does not specify "sensorineural" hearing loss: "I've noticed that the hearing's kind of gone down a bit" without characterization as sensorineural vs conductive.

Bell’s palsy is explicitly mentioned and broader cranial nerve assessment implied: "What you're describing might be something called Bell's palsy" and desire "to do what we call a neurological examination just to make sure there's nothing else going on," i.e., considering other cranial nerve processes.
Assessment acknowledges associated tinnitus and dizziness via the history: patient notes "the ringing occasionally and when I get back and sometimes feel a bit dizzy."
Occupational impact is discussed: "because of all the kind of symptoms... I've just had to do far less training, so kind of beginning to. Yeah. Impacting work a little bit now."

An urgent in-person GP review for neuro exam and otoscopy is planned: "I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today" and "we can do what we call a neurological examination... have a look inside the ear, see if there's anything to see within the ear."
Clinic appointment via admin team: "I'm going to send a message to our admin team. I'll ask them to book you in for a face to face appointment in one of our clinics."

Preliminary reassurance and explanation: "from what you've told me, this doesn't seem to be anything that you're going to die from... preliminarily I can, I can reassure you. However, in order to definitively reassure you, I think you need a physical examination today."

Support team contact details for booking: "then you can ring the support team number. I'll leave that number in your notes. You can ring them after five minutes and then they'll slot you into a place that's convenient for you."
